name: W Trek
summary: The classic 4-night route along the southern face of the massif: Base Torres, Valle del Francés and Glaciar Grey, east to west.
note: Most hikers walk back from Grey to Paine Grande on day 5 for the catamaran across Lago Pehoé.

stages.name: Los Cuernos → Mirador Británico → Paine Grande

name: O Circuit
summary: The full loop around the Paine massif, counter-clockwise, over John Gardner Pass with views down onto the Southern Patagonian Ice Field.
note: Los Perros → Paso is the hardest day: start early, and rangers close the pass in bad weather.

stages.name: Los Perros → John Gardner Pass → Grey

name: Mirador Base Torres
summary: The iconic hike to the three granite towers above a glacial lake. The last hour is a steep boulder scramble.

name: Mirador Cuernos
summary: A flat, windy walk from the Salto Grande trailhead past the waterfall to a close-up view of the Cuernos del Paine across Lago Nordenskjöld.
note: Hold on to your hat: gusts here regularly top 100 km/h.

name: Mirador Cóndor
summary: A short, steep climb from Camping Lago Pehoé to a lookout over Lago Pehoé, Lago Nordenskjöld and the Cuernos. Condors often ride the wind up here.

name: Valle del Francés
summary: Into the heart of the massif: from Paine Grande along Lago Skottsberg to Campamento Italiano, then up beside the hanging Glaciar Francés, which you’ll hear calving, to Mirador Francés.
note: Leave your pack at Campamento Italiano. Rangers close the upper valley after the afternoon cut-off, so check the time at Italiano before heading up.

name: Mirador Lago Grey
summary: Cross the suspension bridge and walk the beach out to the peninsula, where icebergs from Glaciar Grey wash up.

name: Mirador Ferrier
summary: A short, relentlessly steep climb through lenga forest to a panorama over Lago Grey, the glacier and the massif.
